country_overview: Italy is a euro-area member of the European Union. Cross-border movements of cash are administered by the Agenzia delle Dogane e dei Monopoli (ADM), the Italian customs authority, together with the Guardia di Finanza, under Regulation (EU) 2018/1672 for cash entering or leaving the European Union and under Legislative Decree 195/2008 (Article 3) for cash entering or leaving Italian national territory, including movements to and from other EU Member States. The euro is legal tender and Italy applies no national exchange-control approval regime; within the EU legal framework the free movement of capital is guaranteed under Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, subject to Treaty exceptions and to sanctions, anti-money-laundering, tax, reporting and prudential controls rather than exchange controls. Banking, payment and conversion services are provided by intermediaries authorised and supervised by Banca d'Italia within the Eurosystem.

summary.traveler: Travellers carrying cash of EUR 10,000 or more must lodge a declaration with the Italian customs authority (ADM) at the first border customs office. The obligation applies both to cash entering or leaving the European Union (Article 3, Regulation (EU) 2018/1672) and to cash entering or leaving Italian national territory, including movements to or from other EU Member States (Article 3, Legislative Decree 195/2008). 'Cash' covers currency (banknotes and coins), bearer-negotiable instruments, and goods used as highly liquid stores of value such as gold.
summary.business: Italy applies no national exchange-control approval regime; within the EU legal framework the free movement of capital is guaranteed under Article 63 TFEU, subject to Treaty exceptions and to sanctions, anti-money-laundering, tax, reporting and prudential rules. Cross-border payments, foreign-currency accounts and conversion are provided through banks, payment institutions and electronic-money institutions authorised and supervised by Banca d'Italia. Specific resident, non-resident and capital-transfer provisions require claim-specific sourcing.

rules.bring_foreign_currency_in: Cash of EUR 10,000 or more brought into Italy must be declared to the Italian customs authority (ADM) at the first border customs office. Where the traveller enters the European Union through Italy the obligation arises under Article 3 of Regulation (EU) 2018/1672; where the traveller enters Italian national territory from another EU Member State it arises under Article 3 of Legislative Decree 195/2008. 'Cash' includes currency, bearer-negotiable instruments and gold used as a highly liquid store of value.
rules.take_foreign_currency_out: Cash of EUR 10,000 or more taken out of Italy must be declared to the Italian customs authority (ADM) at the first border customs office. The obligation applies on leaving the European Union through Italy (Article 3, Regulation (EU) 2018/1672) and on leaving Italian national territory towards another EU Member State (Article 3, Legislative Decree 195/2008). The same cash categories apply; a declaration with inexact or incomplete information does not satisfy the obligation.
rules.cash_declaration_threshold: The threshold for a mandatory declaration of accompanied cash carried by a traveller is EUR 10,000 or more. Two parallel regimes apply and are administered through a single ADM declaration form: Article 3 of Regulation (EU) 2018/1672 for cash entering or leaving the European Union, and Article 3 of Legislative Decree 195/2008 for cash entering or leaving Italian national territory (including to and from other EU Member States). Unaccompanied cash sent by post, freight or courier is covered separately by Article 4 of Regulation (EU) 2018/1672 (disclosure on the request of customs). Customs may require production of the cash and apply administrative seizure; specific penalty amounts are fixed by Legislative Decree 195/2008.
rules.resident_holding_rules: As a euro-area EU Member State, Italy imposes no national exchange-control approval on residents holding foreign currency or foreign-currency accounts; within the EU legal framework the free movement of capital is guaranteed under Article 63 TFEU, subject to Treaty exceptions and to sanctions, anti-money-laundering, tax, reporting and prudential requirements, exercised through Banca d'Italia-supervised intermediaries.
rules.non_resident_rules: Non-residents may hold accounts and transfer funds through Italian banks and payment institutions without a national exchange-control approval regime, consistent with the free movement of capital under Article 63 TFEU. Account opening and operation remain subject to sanctions screening, anti-money-laundering and identity verification, tax information-reporting, and each institution's own requirements.
rules.business_invoicing_settlement: Cross-border business payments and settlement in euro or foreign currency are executed through banks, payment institutions and electronic-money institutions authorised and supervised by Banca d'Italia, within the EU free-movement-of-capital framework (Article 63 TFEU) and subject to sanctions, anti-money-laundering and reporting rules. Invoice-denomination and specific capital-transfer provisions require claim-specific sourcing.
rules.exchange_controls: Italy maintains no national exchange-control regime. Within the EU legal framework the free movement of capital between Member States and with third countries is guaranteed by Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, subject to the Treaty's own exceptions and to EU restrictive measures (sanctions), anti-money-laundering, tax and prudential rules. This is a Treaty-level framework, not an absence of all rules.
rules.banking_conversion_practicality: Currency conversion and cross-border payments in Italy are provided through banks, payment institutions and electronic-money institutions authorised and supervised by Banca d'Italia, subject to EU and Italian anti-money-laundering, sanctions, tax and prudential controls. Access is widely available through these authorised intermediaries; currency-exchange is a regulated financial activity.

disclaimer: This page provides general informational reference only. Foreign-exchange and cash-control rules in Italy are set by EU and Italian law and may change; requirements depend on residency, the movement concerned (entering/leaving the EU versus Italian national territory), amount, documentation, and the applicable ADM, Banca d'Italia, and EU framework. This is not legal, regulatory, tax, financial, or compliance advice. Always verify current rules directly with the Agenzia delle Dogane e dei Monopoli, Banca d'Italia, or a qualified professional before making any financial or travel decisions.
